title: S301: The Fastest Known Star Orbiting Sagittarius A* and Relativistic Black Hole Entry Dynamics
abstract: S301 is the fastest known star orbiting Sgr A*, reaching 8.5% c (25,600 km/s) at pericenter with e=0.98. A hypothetical civilization at S301 could enter the black hole in ~1.2 days free-fall time. Tidal forces at the event horizon are survivable (0.0012 m/s²) but spaghettification occurs near the singularity. Oberth maneuver at pericenter enables efficient propulsive dives.

c9_implications.quantum_gravity_testbed: Near-singularity regime probes Planck-scale physics. Relevant to Cluster 2 (quantum gravity).
c9_implications.interstellar_trajectory: 1g acceleration reaches near-c in ~1 year (traveler frame). Galactic center reachable in ~10.6 years one-way.
c9_implications.energy_requirements: 55,000x payload rest-mass for 1g to Galactic center. Negative mass/energy density required for zero-cost (Alcubierre-like).
